clue.text: One stirring tea bloke mixed with rum, right?

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of tea bloke and rum are jumbled together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stirring a cuppa that a bloke has laced with rum, asking whether that is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One stirring' looks like a person with a teaspoon; it means someone who stirs up strife.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to provoke discord, and a person who deliberately causes discord is a troublemaker.

clue.text: Model, tense, put up with picture inside

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: inside says the word for picture goes within the word for put
in a down clue up says the word for put is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A tense fashion model tolerating a photograph of herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like the phrase meaning tolerated; it is split, 'put' as LAY, 'up' as the reversal signal in a down clue, and 'with ... inside' as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Model as an adjective means exemplary or representative, the sense of typical in a model case.

clue.text: Date after work for Aida, perhaps

indicators.note: after says the word for date comes behind the one for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period or date in history

explanation.surface: Going out on a date after work to see Aida.
explanation.walkthrough: AIDA is Verdi's opera; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Aida is a well-known example of a sung stage drama.

clue.text: Permit wearing couple's jewellery

indicators.note: wearing says one word has the other on it, so the word for couple's goes around the word for permit

parts.note: a brace is a pair, so couple's gives brace's, written without the apostrophe
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: Someone allowed to wear a pair of jewellery items belonging to a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: BRACE'S reads like a possessive; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracelets are ornaments worn round the wrist, so a form of jewellery.

clue.text: This writer has got upset with student's wickedness

indicators.note: got upset in a down clue says the letters are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves says I've
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: The setter has become upset with a student's misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got upset' turns IVE over to EVI; L is the learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil as a noun is wickedness, moral badness.

clue.text: Most wild adult tigers shot after noon

indicators.note: after says the shuffled tigers follow the letter for noon

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film certificates

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Adult tigers become wildest after being shot in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges TIGERS to GRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild can mean furious, so the most wild person is the most furious, the angriest.

clue.text: Praise former lover to all in the centre

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in the centre says we take the middle letter of all

explanation.surface: Praise an ex-partner to everyone in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or speak very highly of, a synonym of praise.

clue.text: Keep most important article in container

parts.note: main means chief or most important

indicators.note: in says the article is placed inside the container

parts.note: a tin is a container
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instruction to keep the most important item inside a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going or in good order is to maintain it.

clue.text: Fee from cleaner gets reduced by 50 per cent

parts.note: a char is a charwoman, an old British word for a cleaning lady

indicators.note: reduced by 50 per cent says we keep only the first half of gets

explanation.surface: A cleaner's fee has been halved.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR (charwoman) is a British word for a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a price asked for a service, which is a fee.

clue.text: Dressing before shaving

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a shaving is a paring, a thin slice cut off

explanation.surface: Getting dressed in the morning before having a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' is the verb in its sense of getting food ready, as in dressing a salad or a crab.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing a chicken or a salad means getting it ready for cooking or serving, which is preparing it.

clue.text: Refuse tango with dare-devil

parts.note: Tango is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for T
a dare-devil is rash, recklessly bold

explanation.surface: Turning down a tango with a reckless dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is household waste, and trash is the American word for rubbish.

clue.text: Relieved after cold came to an end

indicators.note: after says the word for relieved follows the letter for cold

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
pain that is relieved has been eased

explanation.surface: Something like a pain finally easing off once a cold has run its course.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop, so something that ceased stopped or finished.

clue.text: Hostile and cool on returning after tip from Mad Hatter

indicators.note: after places the hostile, cool and on pieces behind that opening letter
the tip of a word is its first letter, so we take the opening letter of Mad

parts.note: ill can mean unfriendly, as in ill will or ill feeling
in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: returning says the two-letter word for on is read backwards

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Describes the unfriendly, aloof Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' looks like the definition, but 'Mad' only supplies M; 'returning' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatter makes hats, and a milliner is a maker of hats, especially for women.

clue.text: Previous editor continued

parts.note: last means previous, as in last week

explanation.surface: The former editor stayed on in the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lasted went on or endured, the same sense as continued.

clue.text: Small cat hurts no European bears

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: no says the letter for European is dropped from the word for hurts

parts.note: something that hurts aches

explanation.surface: A small cat is hurt by European bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animal; it is the verb, to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, so stomachs means bears or puts up with.

clue.text: Guess I'm stuck in car?

indicators.note: stuck in says the letters of I'm are lodged inside the word for car

parts.note: an estate is a British name for a station wagon, a car with a long rear load space
taken as written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in a car wondering about their situation.
explanation.walkthrough: An ESTATE car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess is a rough judgement of a quantity, which is what an estimate is.

clue.text: Wrong chapter held by rector in training

indicators.note: held by says the letter for chapter sits inside the shuffled letters
training means being drilled and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rector in training got the chapter wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in training' rearranges RECTOR IN, and 'held by' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect means not right, mistaken, which is wrong.

clue.text: Object keeping bosom confined

indicators.note: keeping says the word for object holds the word for bosom

parts.note: an end is an object or aim
a bosom friend is a close friend

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to their chest being kept confined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' is a noun (purpose), and 'bosom' is the adjective of 'bosom friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed means shut in on all sides, so confined.

clue.text: Selecting chinos, go to get changed

indicators.note: to get changed says these letters must be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Picking out a pair of chinos before going off to dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get changed' looks like dressing; it is the anagram signal for CHINOS plus GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Selecting is picking from options, which is choosing.

clue.text: Bird out of one's tree

definitions.meaning: a bird famous for laying eggs in other birds' nests
out of one's tree is slang for crazy

explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo names a European bird and is also informal for mad, like the bird calling from its tree.

clue.text: Beautiful nose almost starts to impede Cleopatra

indicators.note: almost means the word for nose loses its last letter

parts.note: a nose for something is a scent, a sense of smell

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Pascal joked that a shorter Cleopatra's nose would have changed history; here her beautiful nose nearly gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic describes views or landscape that are picturesque, pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Shy ostlers regularly ignored animals

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful

indicators.note: regularly ignored says every other letter of ostlers is dropped, keeping the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Timid stable-hands repeatedly overlooked the animals in their care.
explanation.walkthrough: Ostlers were stable-hands at inns who looked after horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Coyotes are North American wild dogs, so they are animals.

clue.text: Tube stations?

parts.note: the Tube is slang for television, and its stations are TV broadcasting outlets; tubes are also pipes for water

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground, so 'Tube stations' suggests places like Oxford Circus; but 'the tube' also means television, whose stations are these.
explanation.definitionFit: Television stations are known as channels, each a separate broadcast frequency.

clue.text: Relative peace, finally, in French city

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the city

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: finally says we take only the last letter of peace

explanation.surface: A relative finally finds peace in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of a sibling, so a relative.

clue.text: Fairly fair

definitions.meaning: ... as an adverb means fairly or quite, as in ... good
fair in the old sense of beautiful

explanation.definitionFit: Pretty works both as a modifier meaning rather and as an adjective meaning attractive or comely.

clue.text: Image capturing fish in river? On the contrary

indicators.note: capturing, with On the contrary reversing the roles, means the fish holds the river letter

parts.note: a tope is a small shark found in British waters

explanation.surface: A picture of a fish caught in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, 'fish in river' puts TOPE in R; 'On the contrary' flips it so R goes inside TOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, a figurative image used in writing.

clue.text: Wine, not cold, I drink

indicators.note: not says the letter for cold is removed

parts.note: sack is an old word for dry white sherry-type wine, as Falstaff drank

explanation.surface: Someone avoiding chilled wine and drinking it at room temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' looks like a verb but is the noun: saki is a variant spelling of sake.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki, also spelt sake, is Japanese rice wine, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow brooch repaired in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describes a piece of jewellery of a yellowish-brown colour that has been mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment whose colour is a pale brownish yellow.

clue.text: Get away without first attempt at whipping boy

indicators.note: without first means the word for get away loses its opening letter

parts.note: to get away is to escape
a go is an attempt, as in have a go

explanation.surface: A boy escaping before he can be whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping boy was punished for a prince's faults, so the term means someone blamed for others.

clue.text: School leader hides master's blunders

indicators.note: blunders, read as a verb, says these letters stumble into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A head teacher covering up the mistakes made by one of the masters on her staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' reads as a noun, the mistakes being hidden, but works as the anagram signal on HIDES MASTER'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A headmistress is the woman in charge of a school, its head teacher.
